title: Types and Frequency of Enforcement Actions Taken against Errant Active Mobility Device Riders who Speed or Ride on Pathways
what_it_is: Types and Frequency of Enforcement Actions Taken against Errant Active Mobility Device Riders who Speed or Ride on Pathways

sections.label: Enforcement against errant active mobility riders
sections.summary: LTA takes enforcement actions against errant active mobility device riders, uses technology and joint operations, and ensures alternative paths at works sites.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the types and frequency of enforcement actions taken against errant active mobility device riders who speed or ride on pathways where they should not; and (b) whether more resources can be provided for stricter enforcement, especially on pathways affected by infrastructure works in the Central District.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: They also conduct frequent joint enforcement operations with NParks officers in parks and along park connectors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA has also been tapping on technology for enforcement, including a pilot deployment of mobile closed circuit televisions (CCTVs) to catch errant users and identification of hotspots based on public feedback from the MyTransport.SG mobile application.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Offenders caught speeding or using the wrong path, for example, e-scooter or power-assisted bicycle (PAB) riders who use footpaths, are issued with an offence form on the spot.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Where footpaths are affected by infrastructure works, LTA will ensure that alternative crossings or paths are available and signages are installed to guide path users.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: With close to 6,000 kilometres of footpaths and cycling paths islandwide, enforcement alone will not prevent errant behaviour.

sections.label: Enforcement at narrowed paths and works
sections.summary: LTA periodically deploys enforcement officers at narrowed paths, and will work with contractors to reduce disturbance from works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: Because of the works, a lot of the diversion has to take place and, therefore, the paths become a bit narrower than usual and, especially along bus stop areas, where there is a concentration of commuters, cyclists, it does pose a challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: So, with feedback, LTA has been periodically deploying enforcement officers at these areas to look out for errant riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: When the NSC is completed, there will be dedicated active mobility paths where users can enjoy such conveniences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I also note Members' feedback about the works causing noise during certain hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: We will take note and we will work with the contractors to ensure that the works do not cause unnecessary disturbances or inconvenience to the Member's residents.
